data.description:
## Goal

Improve release-gate operability: distinguish an audit-infrastructure failure
(timeout / concurrency / provider error) from a genuine "not ready to close"
verdict, and provide a narrow bypass that skips only in-gate remediation while
still verifying `readyToClose`.

## Why

Today the only escape hatch is `--skip-checks`, which bypasses every gate
(unmerged branches, critical items, worklog refs, producer review, final
validation). Operators facing a slow audit cannot skip just the expensive part.
And "remediation runner failed" is reported alongside genuine failing verdicts,
hiding the real cause.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The audit gates report a distinct reason/category for infra failures
   (timeout/ETIMEDOUT, concurrency limit, provider error) vs genuine failing
   verdicts, and the release output surfaces the category.
2. A narrow flag (e.g. `--skip-audit-remediation`) skips only the in-gate
   remediation attempts while still requiring `readyToClose===true` for every
   in-scope item; it is not forwarded to the merge script.
3. `--skip-checks` behaviour is unchanged.
4. Unit tests cover: infra-failure classification; narrow flag preserves the
   `readyToClose` check and blocks on a genuine failing verdict; flag is
   stripped from forwarded args.
5. Full suite passes; docs updated.
data.title: Ship: distinguish audit-infra failures from genuine verdicts and add a narrow bypass
